description.summary: leave a surface out of screen captures

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client leave one of its own surfaces out of screen captures and recordings while it stays on screen: a tooltip that should not end up in a screenshot of what it points at, for example.
Exclusion is opt-in per surface. Nothing is excluded by default, and no surface is excluded because of its role.
A client can only name its own surfaces, and a surface it leaves out still shows on screen, so the protocol can hide nothing from the user.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: kora_capture_exclusion_manager_v1
interface.description: A global to get a capture exclusion object for a surface.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a capture exclusion object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Informs the server that the client will no longer use this global. Exclusion objects already created stay in effect.

request.name: get_surface_exclusion

description.summary: get the capture exclusion object of a surface

request.description: Creates the object that leaves the surface out of captures. The surface starts included. A surface has at most one such object at a time: asking for a second raises already_constructed.

interface.name: kora_surface_capture_exclusion_v1

description.summary: leaves one surface out of captures

interface.description:
While excluded, the surface and its subsurfaces are drawn on screen but left out of every capture the compositor makes: of an output, of a workspace, and of a toplevel the surface belongs to. Anything the compositor draws for the surface, such as its shadow or the blur behind it, is left out with it, so a capture shows what is underneath. The pointer and drag icons follow the capture's own cursor option instead.
The surface's popups are not excluded with it; they have their own objects.
Once the surface is destroyed, requests other than destroy do nothing.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface is included in captures again from its next commit.

request.name: set_excluded

description.summary: leave the surface out of captures, or put it back

request.description:
Zero includes the surface in captures; any other value leaves it out.
This is double-buffered state, applied on the next wl_surface.commit (for a synchronized subsurface, when its parent's state is applied).

arg.name: excluded
arg.summary: non-zero to leave the surface out
